Lessons.Title: Recording Partial Products: One-digit and Three- or Four-digit Factors
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will multiply a multi-digit number by a one-digit number using an algorithm that uses partial products.
In previous lessons, you used diagrams to represent multiplication of a one-digit number and a whole number of up to four digits. You learned to decompose larger factors by place value and used diagrams and corresponding expressions to support them in finding partial products. In this lesson, you learn an algorithm for keeping track of partial products that come from multiplying the digits of the factors.
Core relationship: Record partial products by place value. Write and sum each place-value contribution when multiplying by one digit.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Which One Doesn’t Belong: Expressions Galore	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  An Algorithm for Noah	 (20 minutes); Activity 2: Try an Algorithm with Partial Products 	 (15 minutes); Cool-down:  Partial Products	 (5 minutes)
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.
